This pull request introduces significant changes to the authentication system and the data model of the application. The most important changes include the addition of new models and relationships, updates to the `AuthController`, and modifications to the database schema to support user preferences for categories, authors, and news sources.

### AuthController Enhancements:
* Added validation rules for user registration to include phone, preferred categories, authors, and sources. Updated the `register` method to handle these preferences and return a `UserResource` with related data.
* Modified the `login` method to delete expired tokens, create a new token with an expiration time, and cache the user data with related preferences.
* Updated the `user` method to cache the authenticated user's details with related preferences.
* Enhanced the `forgotPassword` method to generate a temporary signed URL for password reset and notify the user via email.
* Added a private `syncPreferences` method to handle syncing user preferences for categories, authors, and sources.

### Model Enhancements:
* Added new models: `Author`, `Category`, and `NewsSource` with relationships to `Article` and `User`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-66fd87f03665a33f9eb8ea1d903310936b8aaab3ffbbc8c9ae52ee44721c57b1R1-R26) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-db5d75f027f272af0204a0e836200dbb217b74fc70c7dfa5b6c0cf6af09945c9R1-R26) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5c67642f79b11ba731832709447b704e6a33db0af8ac82f8ce8ebabfd15976f1R1-R27)
* Updated the `Article` model to include relationships with `Category`, `Author`, and `NewsSource`.
* Modified the `User` model to include relationships for preferred categories, authors, and sources, and removed the `preferences` attribute. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-37a2d7d879a7de3f7d73b2975cd22be9f41ec10c334a0dda9ad1e869332e4ecbL26) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-37a2d7d879a7de3f7d73b2975cd22be9f41ec10c334a0dda9ad1e869332e4ecbL49-R66)

### Database Schema Changes:
* Added phone number column to the `users` table.
* Created new tables for `categories`, `article_category`, `category_user`, and similar tables for authors and news sources to support the many-to-many relationships. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f14c11304b2169d7a7212b74ae703ca081511779dab1314cc6ff11347a405beR1-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a8cae0da5ef8867205355267e4ac3dcb232aca5817c38f9d8b3769db370ba7c6R1-R29) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8a6c34ab9259fc0c53ae38bd7205b48f76c08a0eefcab5fb328e599980643336R1-R29)
* Updated the `articles` table to replace `author` and `source_name` with `news_source_id`.

### Configuration Changes:
* Set the token expiration time to 60 minutes in the `sanctum` configuration.

author: ryannedolan
body:
## Summary

When creating a partial view, inherit the row type from the sink table, if one already exists.

## Details

"Partial views" represent pipelines that materialize part of a table. Typically, this table already exists. In that case, we should validate that the pipeline's row type is compatible with the existing sink table's row type.

At the same time, our `CREATE TABLE <sink>` DDL should fully-specify the sink schema -- not the schema of the partial view. Otherwise, Flink connectors are likely to complain that the `CREATE TABLE` DDL does not match what the connector expects.

## Testing

Verified that creating a partial view that is incompatible with an existing sink table will fail to validate:

```
0: Hoptimator> create materialized view ads."AD_CLICKS$part2" as select * from profile.members;
java.lang.AssertionError: Type mismatch: the field sizes are not equal.
AD_CLICKS: RecordType(VARCHAR CAMPAIGN_URN, VARCHAR MEMBER_URN) NOT NULL
pipeline: RecordType(VARCHAR FIRST_NAME, VARCHAR LAST_NAME, VARCHAR MEMBER_URN, VARCHAR COMPANY_URN) NOT NULL
```

A correct partial view works:

```
0: Hoptimator> create materialized view ads."AD_CLICKS$part2" as select member_urn, company_urn from profile.members;
No rows affected (0.44 seconds)
0: Hoptimator> select * from ads."AD_CLICKS$part2";
+-------------------+--------------------------+
|    MEMBER_URN     |       COMPANY_URN        |
+-------------------+--------------------------+
| urn:li:member:123 | urn:li:company:linkedin  |
| urn:li:member:456 | urn:li:company:linkedin  |
| urn:li:member:789 | urn:li:company:microsoft |
+-------------------+--------------------------+
3 rows selected (0.554 seconds)
```

This PR enables `-DTRUST_INCOMING_SIGNAL_HANDLERS=1` to configure _es_ to trust that signal handlers that at startup aren't one of `(SIG_IGN SIG_DFL SIG_ERR)` are valid and shouldn't cause a panic.  Fixes #164.

This enables compiling with certain debugging options like `-pg`, `-fsanitize=address`, or `-fsanitize=memory`.  For example:

```
; make clean es ADDCFLAGS=-pg ADDLDFLAGS=-pg > /dev/null; make test
gcc -o testrun ./test/testrun.c
./es -s < ./test/test.es ./test/tests/*
es panic: initsignals: bad incoming signal value for sigprof: -715ce4c0
make: *** [Makefile:101: test] Error 1

; make clean es ADDCFLAGS='-pg -DTRUST_INCOMING_SIGNAL_HANDLERS=1' ADDLDFLAGS=-pg > /dev/null; make test
gcc -o testrun ./test/testrun.c
./es -s < ./test/test.es ./test/tests/*
file permissions: passed!
file types: passed!
matches match: passed!
redirects redirect: passed!
file globbing: passed!
match/if equivalence: passed!
subjects: passed!
error handling: passed!
es -c: passed!
es -e: passed!
es -p: passed!
es -i: passed!
syntactic sugar: passed!
heredoc sugar: passed!
match sugar: passed!
lexical analysis: passed!
tokenizer errors: passed!
blow the input stack: passed!
umask: passed!
redirections: passed!
exceptions: passed!
heredocs and herestrings: passed!
tilde matching: passed!
flat command expansion: passed!
equal sign in command arguments: passed!
exit status: passed!
wait is precise: passed!
setpgid: passed!
```

This version is relatively quick-and-dirty.  An argument could be made that _es_ shouldn't allow redefining signal handlers that are already defined on startup at all, because we don't know what impact that could have on the calling code.  Or we could get more sophisticated and do the kind of "chained signal handler" concept that libraries like readline do.  I implemented it this way for simplicity -- I don't think that kind of sophistication is warranted unless this is made the default behavior.

# Summary

Implement gradient descent with Armijo Line search following the description of the method in [Numerical Optimization](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-40065-5) page 37.

## Method Description

Let $\theta_k$ be the current iterate, and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R},~\alpha > 0$, $\delta \in (0, 1)$, and $\rho \in (0, 1)$. Then, $\theta_{k+1} = \theta_k - \delta^t \alpha \dot F(\theta_k)$ where $t + 1 \in \mathbb{N}$ is the smallest number such that the following inequality holds

$$F(\theta_k - \delta^t \alpha \dot F(\theta_k)) \leq F(\theta_k) - \rho \delta^t \alpha ||\dot F(\theta_k)||_2^2.$$

## Implementation Details

1. Helper files for conducting line search are included in `src/methods/line_search_helpers`. We separate out this line search and create the functionality so as to re-use the code for non-monotone line search and second order methods requiring line search schemes
2. Backtracking gradient descent (e.g., gradient descent with Armijo line search) is implemented in `src/methods/backtracking_gd.jl`
3. Example files are included using `BacktrackingGD` for least squares, logistic regression, and poisson regression
4. Test cases are provided for the functionality in `src/methods/line_search_helpers`

hopp test src/__tests__/e2e/fixtures/collections/hawk-auth-success-coll.json -e src/__tests__/e2e/fixtures/environments/hawk-auth-envs.json
